before: A transition animates a change between old and new property values. It does not create the state change itself. Here adding the muted class changes opacity; the transition smooths that change when motion is allowed.

transition: opacity 0.08s linear names the property, duration in seconds, and constant-speed timing. opacity: 0.4 makes the whole button partly transparent; it does not disable its action. The reduced-motion media query sets the duration to zero when the person requests reduced motion. The supplied test adds the class, waits for actual animations to finish, checks the endpoint, and removes the class; you only write CSS.

Animate only the opacity change, keep the native button, and provide the zero-duration reduced-motion alternative. after: A transition smooths the change from one CSS value to another. Another rule must cause the change first.
Here, adding the `muted` class changes opacity from 1 to 0.4. Opacity controls how see-through an element is. The button still works when it becomes partly transparent.
Some people ask their device for less motion. The media query respects that choice by making the change instant. The final opacity still changes to 0.4. The checks add and remove the class for you.
